clue.text: Went for private piece by author that is not printed

parts.note: to go for a private soldier is to enlist, that is to have joined up
an author's piece is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone enlisted as a private, and an author produced something that never reached print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'private' looks like secret, but it is the army rank: going for a private means enlisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Cursive handwriting, with linked letters, is the style contrasted with printed letters.

clue.text: City judge putting line through revoked law

indicators.note: putting the line somewhere signals one piece being placed in another
a line put through a word sits inside its letters
a law revoked is turned back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a measure is a law passed by a legislature

explanation.surface: A judge strikes out an old repealed law in some city court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revoked' reads the law backwards, and 'putting line through' sets the L inside it, like a pen stroke across a cancelled statute.
explanation.definitionFit: The holy city is an example of a city, capital of Israel.

clue.text: Sugar controller's rude remark cut short: it starts again

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its last letter

parts.note: an insult is a rude remark
the opening pair of letters, I and N, is repeated at the end, so the word starts again

explanation.surface: Someone controlling a sugar supply is cut off mid-insult, and the row begins again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the T of INSULT; 'it starts again' tells you to repeat its first two letters, IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone made in the pancreas regulates the level of glucose in the blood.

clue.text: Airy, last to believe what actually exists?

indicators.note: the last letter of the word believe is taken

parts.note: what actually exists is the real, as in reality

explanation.surface: A philosophical question: is something airy the last thing to believe in as real?
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to believe' gives E; then THE REAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean light, delicate and insubstantial, like air or the heavens.

clue.text: Release record, Savanna Herd Rounded Up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
the herd animal is placed around the other piece

parts.note: the gnu or wildebeest is an animal of savanna herds
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Reads like a headline: a band releases a record titled Savanna Herd Rounded Up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounded' wraps the gnu round the record, and in a down clue 'Up' reads the result from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg is to free something fastened by a peg, as with prices or a tent.

clue.text: Trail grew doubtful, however magnified

indicators.note: something doubtful is uncertain or unsettled, so the letters are unsettled into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective's trail had become uncertain, but it was magnified nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'however' is a link word introducing the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something shown in an enlarged or exaggerated form.

clue.text: Charge one: being unable to speak, keeping quiet

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: one word keeping another holds it inside

parts.note: unable to speak is mute
P (piano) is the musical abbreviation for quiet

explanation.surface: An accused person stays silent while being charged.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascribe blame or a fault to someone is to charge them with it.

clue.text: Imogen's confession of alcoholism, in one of several forms

parts.note: the setter Imogen refers to herself as I
an admission ..., where to tope is to drink alcohol heavily

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to a drink problem, appearing in one of many guises.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s stands for 'is'; the full confession reads I SO TOPE, 'I so drink to excess'.
explanation.definitionFit: An element can exist as several varieties with different numbers of neutrons, each a separate variant.

clue.text: Argues strenuously, displaying poor judgment

indicators.note: the words on display contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: Someone argues forcefully while showing bad judgment.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimate made without proper evidence is a less than sound judgment.

clue.text: Replaced gold vessel filled with English fruit

indicators.note: the two letters for gold are put back the other way round

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: the vessel is filled with the other piece inside it

parts.note: a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A golden vessel has been swapped for one filled with English fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' here means placed back to front; OR is heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The red seed-pod of a wild rose bush is a hedgerow berry used for syrup.

clue.text: Devilish traditions appeal

parts.note: a little devil is an imp, read here as imp-ish
lore is a body of traditions

explanation.surface: Diabolical customs have a certain attraction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appeal' is a verb here, to beg, not the noun meaning attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg or entreat earnestly is to appeal to someone.

clue.text: Very large note

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
L is the abbreviation for large, on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A huge banknote, or a long loud musical tone.
explanation.definitionFit: In tonic sol-fa this is the fifth degree of the scale, a musical tone.

clue.text: Goalie turns out to make the rules

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered here, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper ends up being the one who sets the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' belongs to the fodder; 'out' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Official rules laid down by an authority are its statutes or directives.

clue.text: An available sum in foreign money no use here?

definitions.text: An available sum in foreign money no use here?

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other, inside its letters

parts.note: lire were the money of Italy
taken as written
cash is money readily available

explanation.surface: A traveller finds foreign currency is no good in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: the county in north-west England uses sterling, so Italian lire are no use there.
explanation.definitionFit: The English county is a place where Italian currency could not be spent.

clue.text: Not unknown for prince to hold drinking bout — a sign of the future?

indicators.note: the prince's name holds the other piece inside
an unknown in algebra is x, y or z; here the y is removed

parts.note: Harry is a British prince
a binge is a drinking bout

explanation.surface: A prince often goes on a drinking spree: an omen of what's to come?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not unknown' drops the Y (an algebraic unknown) from HARRY, leaving HARR, which holds BINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald or forerunner announces or signals something coming.

clue.text: Join the main mass

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: An invitation to become part of the general population.
explanation.definitionFit: The line where two pieces of fabric are stitched together is a joint.

clue.text: One way to get team something in a pie

parts.note: to mince is one way of walking, with affected little steps

indicators.note: the word team is made to get a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: how to get your team something to put in a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Mincing the word 'team' also chops it up into an anagram, a second hint to the same scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiced dried-fruit filling is what fills a traditional Christmas pastry.

clue.text: Pike played by him — a victory, when reeled into the bank

indicators.note: a fish reeled into the bank is drawn inside it, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: a bank is a lender of money
taken as written

explanation.surface: An angler lands a pike onto the riverbank, a win.
explanation.walkthrough: Pike is not the fish: Private Pike in the British TV sitcom Dad's Army was played by the actor Ian Lavender.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor's surname identifies the performer who played that sitcom role.

clue.text: Story young girl lisped

indicators.note: a lisp turns an s sound into th, so the word is spoken with that change

parts.note: a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A little girl lisps her way through telling a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' said with a lisp comes out as 'mith'.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend or traditional tale is a kind of story.

clue.text: Cross with bell regularly interrupting dance

indicators.note: the bell's letters break into the dance, sitting inside it

parts.note: the tango is a dance

indicators.note: every other letter of bell is taken

explanation.surface: An angry person is disturbed by a bell ringing during a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the noun: a hybrid fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit is a citrus cross.

clue.text: Divorced, eh? Good news for one in for the long term

definitions.text: Good news for one in for the long term

parts.note: divorced means free of a spouse
pardon? is a request to repeat, like eh?

explanation.surface: Someone newly divorced hears good news for a long-term partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in for the long term' means serving a long prison sentence, not a long marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A full official forgiveness of an offence releases a prisoner, welcome news to a convict.

clue.text: Ministry to abolish border posts?

parts.note: the prefix de- means to remove, as in de-ice
a fence of posts marks a border

explanation.surface: A government department plans to remove frontier checkpoints?
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's Ministry of Defence is known by its last word, so the department is named.

clue.text: Be about to visit castle, having to change tickets

indicators.note: to visit is to go inside, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: rook is the chess term for a castle

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone about to visit a castle has to change their tickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'castle' is the chess piece, not a building; 'about' turns BE round.
explanation.definitionFit: To book again, for another date, is to alter a reservation.

clue.text: Elegantly decadent discovery: unnamed licensee has been sacked

parts.note: a find is a discovery

indicators.note: sacked means ransacked and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
N is the abbreviation for name, so it is removed

explanation.surface: A discovery: a publican, unnamed, has been fired for decadent behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' drops N from LICENSEE; 'has been sacked' scrambles LICESEE to ESIECLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for 'end of the century' describes the refined decadence of the 1890s.

clue.text: Saying a few words, starts to come apart

indicators.note: saying means spoken aloud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: a phrase is a few words

explanation.surface: Someone speaking briefly begins to fall apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that wears at the edges unravels, beginning to disintegrate.

clue.text: Decipher joke

definitions.meaning: to solve a code is to break it

explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a code and a quip share the same short word in English.

clue.text: Charge less than the whole meal allowance

indicators.note: less than the whole word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a feed is a meal or ration of food

explanation.surface: An expense claim falls short of the full allowance for meals.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment demanded for a service is a charge.

clue.text: Ancient European expelled from a Victorian city

indicators.note: expelled from means taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: Geelong is a city in the Australian state of Victoria

explanation.surface: An elderly European is thrown out of a nineteenth-century city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' means the Australian state, not the era of Queen Victoria.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasting for ages, very long-standing, means very old.

clue.text: A daughter in French port finally off? Not so fast!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the daughter goes in, inside the port's letters
the final letter of the port is taken off

parts.note: Nantes is a port on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: A daughter in a French port is about to leave, and someone urges her to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally off' turns NANTES into NANTE; D goes inside after its first N.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction for a moderate walking tempo asks for a slower pace than allegro.

clue.text: Farm animals doing less well — a blow in expensive area

parts.note: livestock on a farm is stock
doing less well financially means more broke
a belt is a hard blow

explanation.surface: A farmer whose livestock is struggling takes a hit in a pricey district.
explanation.walkthrough: A British term for the wealthy commuter suburbs around London.
explanation.definitionFit: The affluent commuter zone where City financiers live is costly and exclusive.
